The geometric meaning of a vector dot product is the projection of one vector onto another. It can be calculated as the product of the magnitudes of the vectors and the cosine of the angle between them. The dot product is also known as the scalar product or the dot product of vectors.

When two vectors are orthogonal, their dot product is zero. This is because the cosine of 90 degrees is zero. In this case, the vectors are perpendicular to each other and do not overlap. The projection of one vector onto another is the length of the projection of the first vector onto the second vector. This is the length of the vector that is parallel to the second vector.

When the vectors are not orthogonal, the dot product is not zero. The projection of one vector onto another is the length of the projection of the first vector onto the second vector. This is the length of the vector that is parallel to the second vector.

The negative projection of one vector onto another is the length of the projection of the first vector onto the second vector in the opposite direction. This is the length of the vector that is perpendicular to the second vector.

When the vectors are not orthogonal, the dot product is not zero. The negative projection of one vector onto another is the length of the projection of the first vector onto the second vector in the opposite direction.

messages.content:
Return only a complete response. First line TEXT then a concise plain-text answer, or first line UI then the requested specification. For UI an optional second line STATE followed by one space and a JSON object of initial integer inputs is allowed. No fences. No JavaScript, tools, events, HTML or links. One Stack with unique named leaves. Up to 40 leaves, 40 collection members, 64 declarations, depth 32, 16000 UTF-8 source bytes, 10000 frame bytes. Integers for input state. Names start with ASCII letter, then alphanumeric or underscore, at most 48 characters. All declarations must be reachable. Text and labels at most 512 characters. Safe Graphic items use kind plus only required fields: rect(x,y,width,height), circle(cx,cy,r), text(x,y,text), path(d using only M L H V Z, lowercase equivalents, numbers, spaces or commas), group(items of leaves). Numeric coordinates 0..640; viewBox 0 0 450 135.
Return strict JSON with only root (element ID) and elements (object). Root element {"type":"Stack","props":{},"children":["leafId"]}. Each leaf has only type and props. Text props {text}; Metric {label,value}; Control {label,min,max,choices,value:{"$bindState":"/name"}}; Table {values:[{label,score}]}; Graphic {label,items}. Numeric inputs default to minima unless STATE supplies every binding. Read with {"$state":"/name"}. Computations use {"$computed":"Add","args":{"a":number,"b":number}}; Multiply and Excess have the same args, Excess means max(0,a-b). Rank takes args rows (array of [name,[three numeric scores]]), a,b,c (numeric weights) and produces sorted weighted rows. No other functions, properties or nesting of components.
Choose TEXT for a simple definition. Use a legible diagram if spatial relationships aid understanding. Use controls for a changing decision. Label units, state assumptions, use short readable labels, give each output an informative name and check zero or boundary conditions. Keep geometry inside the viewBox.
Example for an unrelated duration converter:
UI
STATE {"hours":1}
{"root":"layout","elements":{"layout":{"type":"Stack","props":{},"children":["knob","minutes"]},"knob":{"type":"Control","props":{"label":"Hours","min":0,"max":12,"choices":[],"value":{"$bindState":"/hours"}}},"minutes":{"type":"Metric","props":{"label":"Minutes","value":{"$computed":"Multiply","args":{"a":{"$state":"/hours"},"b":60}}}}}}
